channel.description: Recent content in Musings on Nithin Kamath's personal homepage

item.title: Introducing Trading from Chart (TFC) on Kite app
item.description: Around 80% of our orders come from mobile. Personally, I still don’t understand how people manage to trade intraday from a phone. 🙂 That said, Trade from Charts (TFC) on mobile has been one of the most requested features. It’s now available on TradingView charts on Kite. With TFC, you can place orders, drag to modify pending orders, and track open positions directly on the chart. Watch this video for more.

item.title: Introducing 4th Cross Labs, our open-source hacker collective
item.description: Our tech team has formed a nice collective that builds and maintains open-source software for public good. The “collective” is just the latest avatar of what we’ve been doing from day one. Over the years, we’ve built and open-sourced tools that are today used by everyone from governments to large companies. I don’t think there’s another company with such a small tech team (~35 people) that has shipped so many side projects that are now world-class, enterprise-grade open-source products.

item.title: The Back Office conversation with Karthik
item.description: I met Karthik Rangappa sometime around 2005. I was trying to sell him an international investing account. I remember going to his office, and we hit it off almost instantly. Later, he helped us build our first website through a friend. This was back when we were called Kamath Associates. He then came to work with us for a bit before going to France to pursue his master’s in finance. He came back and was working on financial education when, in 2013, I reached out and asked him to come build that piece for us.

item.title: Happy 40th, Nikhil
item.description: For many years, people called Nikhil “Nithin.” But over the last 3–4 years, with the success of WTF, I’ve been called Nikhil exponentially more. Forget people just calling me Nikhil in person; I now get emails, LinkedIn messages, tweets, etc., addressed to Nikhil every day.😂​ This popularity was bound to happen. Right from when he was maybe 15 or 16, he was always the guy to go to for anything. He somehow always had connections, and the quality of those connections has only improved over time.

item.title: The first time we appeared in the press
item.description: The first time we appeared in the press was 15 years ago, on September 5th. I first spoke to Nikhil Walavalkar as Sachin, my pseudonym for speaking to clients during sales calls. You didn’t want the CEO making sales calls. 😬 By the way, I’ve even met customers pretending to be Sachin in the early days of Zerodha. Anyway, one day I got a call and picked it up as Sachin.

item.title: The IPO boom and the odds of making listing gains
item.description: While the broader markets have gone nowhere, the primary market (IPOs, OFS, and FPOs) is red hot. By capital raised, this year is already on track to match, if not surpass, the last two years. And there’s a big pipeline of IPOs coming up. Even at Zerodha, there’s been a big spike in IPO applications, including people opening accounts just to apply. If you’re hoping to make easy money from IPOs, the second chart should give you some sense of the odds.

item.title: Account maintenance charges at Zerodha
item.description: A friend asked me if Zerodha charges AMC (Account Maintenance Charges). (Yes, I still get these messages😛). Of Zerodha’s ~2 crore clients, only about around 40% of clients paid AMC during the year. So 60% of our customers don’t pay any AMC because the holdings value of these accounts falls within the BSDA limit. Accounts with holdings less than ₹4 lakh qualify as a Basic Services Demat Account (BSDA). There’s no AMC on a BSDA as long as you only have one demat.

item.title: 16 years of Zerodha
item.description: Zerodha turned 16 this month. Sweet 16. Every year, I write a letter to all our customers about what’s happening in the business and how we are thinking about the future. The last couple of years have been mixed for brokers. We had to take revenue hits because of regulatory changes, and then the Indian market peaked in September 2024. Volumes steadily declined after that, and growth has been muted, to say the least.

item.title: Health insurance checklist for parents
item.description: One of the most basic steps in personal finance is making sure you and your family have adequate health insurance. This is especially important for parents, many of whom bought policies years ago and have kept renewing them even as hospital costs have gone up significantly. Ditto has put together a simple checklist to help you review your parents’ health insurance and figure out whether the cover they have today is actually adequate.

item.title: Intermission by The Ken - Story of ITC
item.description: The fact that ITC started diversifying away from its main tobacco business into hotels and other businesses after almost 70 years of existence was an immense feat of foresight. Especially considering ITC was never a founder-driven company. They knew tobacco was extremely harmful to health and addictive. When something is bad for people but difficult to ban outright, governments invariably keep regulating and taxing it more. Over time, the taxes become so high and the revenues so significant that the government itself ends up in a strange place: ban it or continue taxing it?

item.title: Answering questions about Zerodha’s approach to F&O and MTF
item.description: This discussion on Tradingqna started with a question about retail participation in derivatives, why F&O volumes are falling, and how we are thinking about business diversification. This then became a philosophical discussion about why we offer F&O and MTF, and whether we are compromising on our values by offering products like MTF. These are questions I get asked often: “You keep speaking about the philosophies of Zerodha, how you guys give back, etc.

item.title: What will the future of investing and trading look like?
item.description: If you think about it, trading and investing have changed a lot on the surface, but the fundamental act has remained more or less the same. Platforms look better. They are easier to use. There is more information, more data, more products, and far better tools. But underneath all of that, you still place an order through a broker, which then goes to an exchange. The question we keep asking ourselves at Zerodha and Rainmatter is: will this remain true in the future?

item.title: Making it easier for NRIs to invest in India
item.description: I’ve spoken many times about the need to make it easier for NRIs to invest in India. Finally, some great news. SEBI just released a consultation paper proposing a fully digital onboarding process for NRIs, without needing them to be physically present in India! Kudos to SEBI for this pragmatic move. This is huge because NRIs tend to have large amounts of capital to invest and are a highly durable source of inflows into Indian markets.

item.title: The Back Office with Venu Madhav
item.description: I still wonder what made Venu Madhav call me back in 2006 to ask, “Is there something I can do?” At the time, there was zero line of sight, I couldn’t even guarantee him a monthly salary. Yet he walked away from a stable, well-paying job at HP to join me back when I was just a sub-broker at Reliance Money😬 Zerodha wouldn’t be Zerodha today without him running pretty much all of our operations, compliance, and more over the years.

item.title: AI is no longer a differentiator
item.description: The number of investment decks I get leading with “we use AI” is ridiculous. It’s reached a point where it automatically makes my eyes roll, and I’ve almost stopped looking at them. Founders need to realize that AI is just table stakes now. Bragging that your product uses AI is like bragging that you take a bath every day. It’s not a differentiator. In fact, opening your pitch with it is a surefire way to get ignored, not just by us, but by most serious VCs.

item.title: Rainmatter Originals - The story of Akshayakalpa
item.description: What this country needs is more businesses that try to do more than just business, businesses that give back to the communities and ecosystems they depend on. In that sense, we need more businesses that don’t just take value from the system, but actively put value back into it. Akshayakalpa is one of them, and that’s one of the reasons we invested. Shashi and the team are building a business for profit, of course, but profit isn’t the only motivation.

item.title: Making fitness more participatory with peakst8
item.description: Given my passion for all things health, I keep getting into all sorts of activities that I probably shouldn’t, considering my age. Yesterday, the team and I were trying a new hybrid fitness format called No Parking. It wasn’t as challenging as Hyrox, but it definitely wasn’t a cakewalk either. My heart rate shot up quickly with push-ups, rowing, sit-ups, and mountain climbers, while my teammate Deepak did all the activities that involved running😄

item.title: To run a brokerage firm is to live with contradictions
item.description: To run a brokerage firm is to live with contradictions. Especially if you have a fine-tuned moral and ethical compass.😬 By far the biggest contradiction I live with is around leverage. I was thinking about this because Mridul Arora asked me about it recently, and I couldn’t answer it as well as I wanted to on the spot. For years, I’ve spoken about the dangers of leverage. Yet we’re probably one of the businesses that has benefited the most from it, whether through intraday trading, F&O, or now MTF.

item.title: The problem with borrowing for lifestyle spending
item.description: Taking a loan has never been easier. There is almost no friction between wanting something and borrowing to pay for it. The problem is that income is limited, while the list of things we want is endless. And often, it isn’t even the purchase we want as much as the momentary thrill of buying it. We are taught how to earn and save, but learning how to spend is just as important.

item.title: Introducing all-new SIP flow on Kite web
item.description: A lot of Zerodha customers don’t know that you can set up SIPs for stocks and ETFs, just like mutual funds. SIPs are probably the easiest way to bring some discipline to investing. We’ve had Stock SIPs on Kite for a while, but the process of setting one up could have been better. We’ve now introduced an all-new Stock SIP flow on Kite web. You can add stocks or ETFs while creating an SIP, choose between quantity-based and amount-based SIPs, and allocate the investment amount across multiple stocks or ETFs.
